A car covers 120 km in 2 hours, then stops for 1 hour, then covers a further 60 km in 1 hour. (a) Find the speed of the car during the first 2 hours. (b) Find its average speed for the whole journey.
items.answer: (a) 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.  (b) 180 km in 4 hours, so 45 km/h.

items.prompt: Simplify 4a + 7b - 2a + 3b.
Simplify 3x × 4x.
Simplify 18m²n ÷ 6mn.
Simplify x/3 + x/6.
Which of these is 4a - 12 written as a product?
Factorise 6x + 9.
Factorise x² + 5x.
The area of a rectangle is x² + 7x square centimetres. Factorise the expression, and give a possible length and width of the rectangle.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 2 marks for x(x + 7); 2 marks for a correct pair, e.g. length (x + 7) cm and width x cm (the two may be given the other way round).

items.prompt: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the alternate angles are
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of the angles is 68°. Find (a) its corresponding angle, (b) its alternate angle.
items.answer: (a) 68°  (b) 68° - corresponding and alternate angles between parallel lines are equal.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle of 115° and its co-interior angle lie on the same side of the transversal. Find the size of the co-interior angle.
Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only, construct an angle of 120° and then bisect it. Measure and state the size of each of the two parts.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 2 marks for the arcs that give 120° (two 60° steps, or a 60° angle with its adjacent 60°); 2 marks for the bisecting arc and ray; 1 mark for stating that each part is 60°.

items.prompt: An angle of 135° is bisected. What is the size of each part?
Construct a triangle with sides 6 cm, 5 cm and 4 cm. Measure its largest angle and state whether the triangle is acute-angled or obtuse-angled.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 2 marks for a base drawn to one of the given lengths; 2 marks for the two arcs locating the third vertex; 1 mark for the largest angle, which is about 83°, so the triangle is acute-angled.

items.prompt: What is the size of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
A triangle has two sides of 7 cm and the angle between them is 60°. What type of triangle is it?
items.answer: An equilateral triangle - the third side is also 7 cm.

items.prompt: The locus of the points that are equidistant from two intersecting straight lines is
options: the two lines parallel to them
a circle through the crossing point
the perpendicular bisector of the lines
the two lines that bisect the angles between them
items.answer: the two lines that bisect the angles between them

items.prompt: Describe the locus of a point that moves so that it is always 4 cm from a fixed point O.
items.answer: A circle of radius 4 cm with centre O.

items.prompt: Describe the locus of the points that are equidistant from two fixed points A and B.
items.answer: The perpendicular bisector of the line segment AB.

items.prompt: Construct a line segment AB of length 6 cm. Draw the locus of the points that are equidistant from A and B, and the locus of the points that are 5 cm from A. Mark the two points where the loci meet.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 2 marks for the perpendicular bisector of AB; 2 marks for the circle of radius 5 cm with centre A; 1 mark for marking the two points where the circle crosses the bisector.

options: the same magnitude and the same direction
items.answer: the same magnitude and the same direction

items.prompt: The vector from P(1, 2) to Q(5, 1) is (4, -1). The vector from R(0, 3) to S(4, 2) is also (4, -1). What can you say about the two vectors?
items.answer: They are equal vectors: they have the same magnitude and the same direction, so they are also parallel.

items.prompt: The turning of the hands of a clock is an example of
Give two examples of rotation in everyday life.
items.answer: Any two, e.g. the hands of a clock, a ceiling fan, a wheel, a windmill, the opening of a door.

A figure and its image under a rotation have the same size and the same shape. What name is given to two figures like this?
Two figures are congruent if
options: they have the same area but different shapes
they have the same perimeter but different shapes
they have the same shape and the same size
they have the same shape but different sizes
items.answer: they have the same shape and the same size

items.prompt: Two rectangles measure 3 cm by 4 cm and 6 cm by 8 cm. Are they similar? Give a reason.
items.answer: Yes. 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the sides are in the same ratio and the shapes are the same.

items.prompt: A map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 500. A rectangular field measures 4 cm by 3 cm on the map. Find the real dimensions of the field in metres.
Which of the following gives categorical data?
options: The weights of the school bags in kilograms
The ages of the pupils in years
The favourite colours of the pupils in a class
The heights of the pupils in centimetres
items.answer: The favourite colours of the pupils in a class

items.prompt: Data arranged in class intervals such as 10 - 19, 20 - 29 is called
State whether each of the following is numerical or categorical data: (a) shoe sizes (b) favourite food (c) number of brothers and sisters.
The best way to find the number of vehicles that pass a junction between 7 a.m. and 8 a.m. is to
options: interview the drivers of the vehicles
send a questionnaire to the drivers
carry out an experiment on the vehicles
observe the junction and tally the vehicles
items.answer: observe the junction and tally the vehicles

items.prompt: You want to find the number of people living in each house in your community. Which method would you use to collect the data, and why?
items.answer: A survey - a house-to-house count or a questionnaire - because the information has to be collected from each house and then added up.

items.answer: Marks 4: 1 pupil; 5: 1; 6: 3; 7: 4; 8: 4; 9: 2. The frequencies must add up to 15.
